newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF MONACO V MARSEILLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MATCH ANALYSIS OF MONACO V MARSEILLE.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Monaco and Marseille ahead of their French first division meeting on Saturday at the Louis II stadium (kick-off 1800 GMT).

Playing style: At home, Monaco usually line up with three in defence, Patrick Blondeau who was capped by France for the first time aged 29 this year, captain Franck Dumas and Martin Djetou. In midfield, which could be four or five strong, playmaker Ali Benarbia is back after missing Monaco's UEFA Cup elimination at the hands of Internazionale in midweek because of suspension. The attack is usually two-pronged with Brazilian Anderson and teenager Thierry Henry almost certain to link up on Saturday as Victor Ikpeba is away on World Cup duty with Nigeria.

Strengths: The strongest squad in the French league, which has helped Monaco make light of injury to several first choice players earlier in the season. Variety of scoring options with Anderson on 17 league goals, Ikpeba on 11 and Henry on eight. A coach, Jean Tigana, strong on motivation who guided Monaco into the UEFA Cup semifinals with some brilliant counter-attacking football in the away legs although they lost in Milan for the first time in their semifinal against Internazionale.
Weaknesses: Small home crowds that create little atmosphere at Monaco's Louis II stadium. Divisions in the squad that have surfaced since the defeat in Milan and undermined confidence.

Motivation: A sixth league title and first since 1988, when they triumphed under Arsene Wenger. They came close last year after a poor first half of the season and have since strengthened their squad.
Team (probable): Fabien Barthez, Patrick Blondeau, Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou, Lilian Martin, Gilles Grimandi, Emmanuel Petit, Sylvain Legwinski, Ali Benarbia, Anderson, Thierry Henry.

Playing style: Marseille play with a classic back four away that needs some adjusting in the light of Italian central defender Ivan Franceschini's unavailability through injury. They tend to play through the middle of midfield looking for the shortest route to strikers Xavier Gravelaine and Marc Libbra.

Strengths: The talent of some of their players, capable of very good performances on their day, such as Germany's goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, although he is in doubt through injury, and local boys Hamada Jambay at the back, Olivier Echouafni in midfield and Libbra up front.

Weaknesses: Marseille have yet to win away this season and are haunted by the possibility of equalling the record of their 1958/9 side which ended the season without a victory on the road although they are not in danger of relegation like their predecessors. A thin squad that club president Robert Louis-Dreyfus has pledged himself to strengthen for next season when, he said, "if Marseille don't finish in the top five in the championship I will have failed."

Motivation: Ending the run of no away wins and continuing their good results against the leading teams which included a 3-1 home win over Monaco in November. The victory sparked a six-match unbeaten run in the league for Marseille, but actually did Monaco even better as they went on to take over from Paris St Germain at the top and did not lose again until late February.
Team (probable): Andreas Koepke, Chris Makin, Christophe Galtier, Hamada Jambay, Jean-Christophe Marquet, Bernard Ferrer, Olivier Echouafni, Eric Roy, Yordan Lechkov, Xavier Gravelaine, Marc Libbra.
